premise: I drained my $112,000 widow’s inheritance to buy a historic quilt-fabric shop with my daughter-in-law, who notarized a 50/50 partnership and promised me a lifetime teaching role, but after a fabric company offered $650,000 for the vintage patterns she forged a dissolution, sold everything, and mailed me a $3,500 “gratitude” check; I discovered the original agreement stitched inside a quilted wall hanging I had made, proved the fraud, and now run “Stitch of Betrayal Quilts,” where she hand-labels every quilt with “I Unraveled Family Trust” and her garnished wages fund a women’s shelter sewing program.
